title: Constant Force Motion in One Direction
learningObjectives: Calculate 1D acceleration from net force and mass using a = F/m.
Explain net force as the difference of opposing forces in 1D motion.
Predict velocity and position over time under constant acceleration.

sources.title: Equations of Motion — NASA Glenn Research Center, Beginner's Guide to Aeronautics

explanations.text: For constant mass, acceleration equals net force divided by mass.

evidence.quote: The force (F) will be the difference between the opposing forces (thrust minus drag).
However, if the forces become unbalanced, the aircraft will move in the direction of the greater force.

explanations.text: Net force in one direction is the difference of opposing forces, and unbalanced force causes motion toward the greater force.

evidence.quote: For a constant force and constant mass, the acceleration remains constant.
Note that these equations can be used only if the mass and the force (and the acceleration) are constant.

explanations.text: Constant force and constant mass produce constant acceleration, and the motion equations apply only in that case.
Under constant acceleration, velocity grows linearly with time and position follows the time-squared relation.

predictions.prompt: A model aircraft of mass 4 kg has a net horizontal force of 12 N. Predict its acceleration.
A model aircraft of mass 5 kg has a net horizontal force of -10 N. Predict its acceleration.
A model aircraft of mass 2.5 kg has a net horizontal force of 5 N. Predict its acceleration.
